_protocol: arXiv:2601.11578 sec 3.3 -- ground truth for coverage evaluation
_composition: The paper builds ground truth by merging author-stated limitations with weaknesses mined from OpenReview reviewer comments (10-12 per paper). The OpenReview half is UNAVAILABLE in this environment: api2.openreview.net returns HTTP 403 on forum queries and the forum page is a JavaScript shell. The reviews demonstrably exist (ICLR 2025 Poster, forum j1tSLYKwg8); this is an access failure, not an absence. Ground truth here is therefore the author-stated half only.
_tautology_warning: Author-stated ground truth overlaps the Extractor Agent's task by construction. Coverage of this ground truth is therefore near-tautological for any pipeline containing an Extractor, and is NOT evidence of the multi-agent framework's value. It is reported because it is the paper's protocol, and its weakness is stated rather than hidden. The discriminating comparison is the zero-shot baseline, which shares the same advantage.
_extracted_by: Independent pass over litreview/data/anchor_fulltext.txt, not read from agent output.

items.text: Models are trained on 30B-70B tokens which may be insufficient to preserve general knowledge from the original LM.
DiffuLLaMA's performance falls short of the LLaMA2 model it was adapted from.
The model does not show signs of saturation; more training tokens are expected to improve results.
Withholding suffix information from baselines might result in an unfair infilling comparison.
Instruction tuning is left as future work.
Adding chain-of-thought to in-context examples drops performance, attributed to absence of instruction tuning.
The model exhibits high uncertainty about its responses, causing suboptimal performance.
Attention mask annealing is omitted at 7B to simplify implementation with flash-attention 2.
The [MASK] token reuses an existing vocabulary word instead of expanding the vocabulary, for implementation reasons.
Direct ablation on adaptation training is too costly, so recipe decisions rest on cheaper preliminary experiments.
TriviaQA and PIQA are challenging for the models because they require specific factual/physical knowledge.
DiffuGPT's training budget does not match GPT2's ~200B tokens.
